claim.why_it_matters: A tool or reader that walks the heading outline places the USAGE clause (and its syntax and general rules) inside the SYNCHRONIZED clause section, so a section lookup for 5.14 or a citation anchor derived from the outline resolves wrongly.
claim.note: Heading at the wrong level: its siblings 5.13 THE SYNCHRONIZED CLAUSE (page 276) and 5.15 THE VALUE CLAUSE (page 280) are '##' with '###' subsections, but 5.14 is '###' and its subsections 5.14.1-5.14.4 are '####', so 5.14 nests under 5.13 in the document outline.

verdict.reasoning: Confirmed in specs/ANSI_COBOL_1985.md: line 11657 '## 5.13 THE SYNCHRONIZED CLAUSE' (subsections '###'), line 11727 '### 5.14 THE USAGE CLAUSE' with 5.14.1-5.14.4 at '####' (lines 11729-11760), line 11792 '## 5.15 THE VALUE CLAUSE' (subsections '###'). The printed page VI-46 shows '5.14 THE USAGE CLAUSE' as a top-level clause heading in the same style as 5.13 and 5.15, a sibling by numbering. The heading text is present, so this is not a missing heading but a heading demoted one level, which nests the whole USAGE clause under 5.13 in the outline. Structural, not textual.
verdict.corrected_description: Not missing: the 5.14 heading and its four subsections are each one level too deep ('###'/'####' instead of '##'/'###'), so 5.14 nests under 5.13 SYNCHRONIZED in the markdown outline.
